questions.question: If two cars travel the exact same distance of 10 miles, but Car A has a higher speed than Car B, what can we say about the time taken by Car A?
options: Car A takes more time than Car B
Car A takes less time than Car B
Both cars take the same amount of time
Car A does not take any time

questions.question: Which of the following formulas is used to calculate the speed of a moving object?
options: Speed = distance x time
Speed = time / distance
Speed = distance / time
Speed = distance + time

questions.question: Which of the following is a standard unit of speed?
options: Metres per second (m/s)
Seconds per metre (s/m)
Kilograms per hour (kg/h)
Newtons per second (N/s)

questions.question: What is the direct effect of a non-zero resultant force acting on a moving object?
options: It always makes the object turn left
It can change the speed of the object
It keeps the speed of the object perfectly constant
It increases the mass of the object

questions.question: When looking at a distance-time graph, what does a steeper line (greater gradient) indicate about the movement of an object?
options: The object is moving slower
The object is stationary
The object is moving faster
The object is moving backward

questions.question: Under what condition does a falling object reach terminal velocity?
options: When the drag force is greater than the gravitational force
When the gravitational force is twice the drag force
When the drag force and gravitational force are equal
When there is no drag force acting on the object

questions.question: How does increasing the surface area of a parachute affect its drag force?
options: It reduces the drag force
It makes the drag force bigger
It has no effect on the drag force
It reduces the gravitational pull to zero

questions.question: When a skydiver with a parachute is falling at their top speed (terminal velocity), how does the drag force compare to the force of gravity on the jumper?
options: The drag force is larger than gravity
The drag force is smaller than gravity
The drag force is the same size as gravity
There is no drag force at top speed

questions.question: What does a horizontal, level line represent on a distance-time graph?
options: An object moving at a constant high speed
An object that is stationary
An object that is accelerating rapidly
An object moving back to its starting point

questions.question: On a distance-time graph, what do upward-sloping and downward-sloping lines represent?
options: Movement at the same speed in the same direction
Movement in opposite directions
The object is accelerating and then stopping
The object is getting heavier and then lighter

questions.question: What is meant by the 'instantaneous speed' of a vehicle?
options: The speed of the vehicle calculated over an entire journey
The maximum speed the vehicle can possibly reach
The speed of the vehicle at a particular moment in time
The speed of the vehicle when it is stationary

questions.question: Why do scientists take repeat readings during an experiment on motion?
options: To increase the amount of systematic error
To reduce the effect of random errors
To make the experiment take longer
To change the physical properties of the object

questions.question: In which direction does the force of friction always act on a moving object?
options: In the same direction as the movement
Directly downwards towards the Earth
Against the direction of movement
Directly upwards away from the ground

questions.question: According to physics principles, what will happen to an object moving at a steady speed in a straight line if no resultant force acts on it?
options: It will gradually slow down and stop
It will continue to move at that steady speed in a straight line
It will suddenly speed up
It will immediately turn in a circle

questions.question: What is the main benefit of designing an object to be streamlined?
options: It increases the mass of the object
It reduces drag
It increases the gravitational force on it
It prevents friction from acting entirely

questions.question: How does the drag force on an object moving through a fluid (like air or water) change as its speed increases?
options: The drag force decreases
The drag force remains completely constant
The drag force increases
The drag force drops to zero
